note: Recorded on 2026-08-10 against the Cloud sandbox, unmodified beyond JIRA_RECORD_SCRUB and the response-header filter in transport.KeptHeaders, which drops every header no code reads. The request in epicadd.cloud.json, sent to a team-managed (next-gen) project and refused with 400. It is kept because a fix that stops sending it needs the reason to survive: team-managed is the default for every new Cloud project, and without this the endpoint reads as simply correct. The response body carries a developer.atlassian.com link, which the residue check reports as an undeclared host; it is Jira's own documentation URL and not a leak.

response.body: {"errorMessages":["The request contains a next-gen issue. This operation can't add next-gen issues to epics. To add a next-gen issue to an epic, use the Edit issue operation and set the parent property (i.e., '\"parent\":{\"key\":\"PROJ-123\"}' where \"PROJ-123\" has an issue type at level one of the issue type hierarchy). See developer.atlassian.com for more details."],"errors":{}}
